correctness.rationale: For odd target lengths the two complementary alternating palindromes each have k runs and opposite starts, forcing k+1 host runs; for even lengths the complementary central-double alternators each have k-1 runs, forcing k host runs. The exactly counted arch decompositions after removal of the first zero or last one of the explicit W_k ensure all length-(k-1) binary suffix/prefix patterns occur; palindrome endpoints reduce all test patterns to those two cases. Witnesses have exactly 2ceil(k/2) runs and length 2k; 0^k and 1^k give the length bound. Fixed-run capacity follows by inversion and appending one zero. Actual verify.py passed for k<=28, every host n<=12, and constructions r<=36; finite checks corroborate but do not replace the universal proof.

value.rationale: This solves the exact host-run resource for the complete palindrome-subsequence test family at every order (a natural restricted spectrum), obtains simultaneous minimum host length 2k and minimum 2ceil(k/2) runs with constructive witnesses, and exposes a sharp parity split relative to full-spectrum universality. It is an infinite structural extremal theorem rather than a finite experiment, routine enumeration of a known table, or substitution into the full-universality law; it can inform design of low-run covering words under palindrome-restricted subsequence tests.
